samples.prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=visual_security; abstract_task=industrial_logic_and_compliance. Task objective: test industrial_logic_and_compliance capability inside the visual_security industrial domain. Scene family: vsec_unregistered_vehicle_intrusion. Core scenario: Unregistered third-party truck enters a marked restricted industrial zone; show detection, alarm, and security response. Reference subject: industrial gate vehicle restricted zone. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: hold a fixed monitoring view; no camera movement; target motion value 0.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Gate, loading dock, factory road, or restricted lane with clear vehicle path and access boundary. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Application value layer: application_type=safety_training. Application objective: Train or evaluate recognition of unsafe industrial states, violations, alarms, and required safe responses. Scenario: Unregistered third-party truck enters a marked restricted industrial zone; show detection, alarm, and security response. Required observable events: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: industrial gate vehicle restricted zone; the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active. Decision-relevant elements: worker or vehicle position relative to the danger zone (industrial gate vehicle restricted zone); PPE, barrier, signage, interlock, or alarm state; machine state before and after the trigger; reference-image requirement: Gate, loading dock, factory road, or restricted lane with clear vehicle path and access boundary. Application success criteria: a safety reviewer can identify the violation and the required response; the event sequence is complete enough for training or compliance audit; the clip does not invent misleading safe states after a hazardous trigger. Misleading failure modes to penalize: hazard appears without the required alarm or stop consequence; unsafe action is visually softened so the violation becomes ambiguous; scene adds irrelevant people or equipment that changes the decision context.

Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Mobile crane, tower crane, or suspended hook/load with visible exclusion zone. samples.prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=visual_security; abstract_task=topology_mutation_and_failure. Task objective: test topology_mutation_and_failure capability inside the visual_security industrial domain. Scene family: vsec_perimeter_fence_breach. Core scenario: Restricted-zone fence is broken by impact; only the damaged section opens while the rest of the barrier stays fixed. Reference subject: industrial perimeter fence gate. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a controlled dolly-in toward the local defect or failure region; target motion value 1.5. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Industrial fence, gate, barrier, or guardrail with localized area for damage. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.80, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.05, reference_and_motion_fidelity=1.35, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=safety_training. Application objective: Train or evaluate recognition of unsafe industrial states, violations, alarms, and required safe responses. Scenario: Restricted-zone fence is broken by impact; only the damaged section opens while the rest of the barrier stays fixed. Required observable events: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: industrial perimeter fence gate; the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active. Decision-relevant elements: worker or vehicle position relative to the danger zone (industrial perimeter fence gate); PPE, barrier, signage, interlock, or alarm state; machine state before and after the trigger; reference-image requirement: Industrial fence, gate, barrier, or guardrail with localized area for damage. Application success criteria: a safety reviewer can identify the violation and the required response; the event sequence is complete enough for training or compliance audit; the clip does not invent misleading safe states after a hazardous trigger. Misleading failure modes to penalize: hazard appears without the required alarm or stop consequence; unsafe action is visually softened so the violation becomes ambiguous; scene adds irrelevant people or equipment that changes the decision context.

[EVENT] Show: Restricted-zone fence is broken by impact; only the damaged section opens while the rest of the barrier stays fixed Common failure modes to AVOID: identity_swap; global_scene_regeneration; implausible_motion_or_flow. samples.prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=visual_security; abstract_task=industrial_logic_and_compliance. Task objective: test industrial_logic_and_compliance capability inside the visual_security industrial domain. Scene family: vsec_pedestrian_forklift_near_miss. Core scenario: Pedestrian enters forklift lane; show warning, braking, and near-miss avoidance without identity swaps. Reference subject: warehouse forklift pedestrian lane. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: hold a fixed monitoring view; no camera movement; target motion value 0.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Warehouse aisle or yard intersection with forklifts/pedestrian route and readable right-of-way context. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Application value layer: application_type=safety_training. Application objective: Train or evaluate recognition of unsafe industrial states, violations, alarms, and required safe responses. Scenario: Pedestrian enters forklift lane; show warning, braking, and near-miss avoidance without identity swaps. Required observable events: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: warehouse forklift pedestrian lane; the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active. Decision-relevant elements: worker or vehicle position relative to the danger zone (warehouse forklift pedestrian lane); PPE, barrier, signage, interlock, or alarm state; machine state before and after the trigger; reference-image requirement: Warehouse aisle or yard intersection with forklifts/pedestrian route and readable right-of-way context. Application success criteria: a safety reviewer can identify the violation and the required response; the event sequence is complete enough for training or compliance audit; the clip does not invent misleading safe states after a hazardous trigger. Misleading failure modes to penalize: hazard appears without the required alarm or stop consequence; unsafe action is visually softened so the violation becomes ambiguous; scene adds irrelevant people or equipment that changes the decision context.

samples.prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=embodied_robotics; abstract_task=rigid_body_kinematics_and_coupling. Task objective: test rigid_body_kinematics_and_coupling capability inside the embodied_robotics industrial domain. Scene family: erob_amr_warehouse_navigation. Core scenario: AMR navigates around pallets with physically plausible wheel path and stable chassis geometry. Reference subject: autonomous mobile robot warehouse. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a smooth constant-radius orbit around the subject; target motion value 45.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Autonomous mobile robot or AGV in warehouse aisle with shelves or pallet stations. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.70, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.45, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.85, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. Scenario: AMR navigates around pallets with physically plausible wheel path and stable chassis geometry. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: autonomous mobile robot warehouse; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (autonomous mobile robot warehouse); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: Autonomous mobile robot or AGV in warehouse aisle with shelves or pallet stations. Application success criteria: a robotics user can judge whether the operation is feasible; motion respects kinematic limits, contact, and collision constraints; task progress is local and does not mutate unrelated scene structure. Misleading failure modes to penalize: robot links bend, detach, or pass through objects; tool or workpiece identity changes during manipulation; requested operation is replaced by camera drift or static display.

Core scenario: Robot applies tool contact force to a workpiece; avoid tool penetration, floating force, and surface drift. Reference subject: robot sanding welding tool contact. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a slow horizontal pan while the mechanism operates; target motion value horizontal_pan_lr. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Robot sanding, welding, drilling, or polishing tool in contact with surface. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.70, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.45, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.85, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. Scenario: Robot applies tool contact force to a workpiece; avoid tool penetration, floating force, and surface drift. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: robot sanding welding tool contact; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (robot sanding welding tool contact); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: Robot sanding, welding, drilling, or polishing tool in contact with surface. Application success criteria: a robotics user can judge whether the operation is feasible; motion respects kinematic limits, contact, and collision constraints; task progress is local and does not mutate unrelated scene structure. Misleading failure modes to penalize: robot links bend, detach, or pass through objects; tool or workpiece identity changes during manipulation; requested operation is replaced by camera drift or static display.

[SCENE] Crane outrigger pad sinks into soft ground, changing support state while boom and chassis stay coherent

[APPLICATION] Industrial use case: heavy_operation_risk. Application objective: Assess whether heavy equipment, loads, supports, and worksite risks evolve plausibly for planning and supervision. Scenario: Crane outrigger pad sinks into soft ground, changing support state while boom and chassis stay coherent. Required observable events: load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: crane outrigger support pad; the requested operation or failure progression occurs; final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation. Decision-relevant elements: load path, rigging, outrigger, support, ground, or bridge alignment (crane outrigger support pad); clearance to workers, vehicles, obstacles, or exclusion zones; motion direction, contact points, and structural deformation cues; reference-image requirement: Crane outrigger, support pad, soft ground, or temporary foundation. Usable only if: a site engineer can infer whether the operation remains safe; gravity, support, load transfer, and contact are physically credible; critical geometry and worksite context stay stable across frames.

[CAMERA] DOLLY FORWARD into the scene along the central axis, starting from the reference-image viewpoint. Maintain subject framing throughout.

[EVENT_LOOP] Complete event loop: 1) initial stable industrial state; 2) trigger or abnormal condition; 3) visible event progression; 4) correct industrial consequence or response; 5) final state consistent with the scenario.

[EVENT] Show: Crane outrigger pad sinks into soft ground, changing support state while boom and chassis stay coherent Common failure modes to AVOID: identity_swap; global_scene_regeneration; implausible_motion_or_flow. The specified structural change must be localized to the failure zone. All surrounding geometry remains stable.

[PRESERVE] Subject identity: crane outrigger support pad. Component counts must remain constant in all non-failure regions. Background, lighting, and layout must stay identical to the reference image. Material textures, surface markings, and color must not drift between frames.

[PROHIBIT] No text overlays, subtitles, logos, or watermarks. No extra machines, vehicles, or people appearing without cause. No geometry warping, melting, or flickering. No identity swaps or model changes mid-clip. No impossible physics: floating loads, rigid bodies bending, penetration, or unsupported motion. No global scene regeneration; changes must stay local to the specified event zone.

samples.prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=heavy_load_construction; abstract_task=topology_mutation_and_failure. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a controlled dolly-in toward the local defect or failure region; target motion value 1.5. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Crane outrigger, support pad, soft ground, or temporary foundation. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.80, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.05, reference_and_motion_fidelity=1.35, temporal_consistency=1.25. Core scenario: Pedestrian enters forklift lane; show warning, braking, and near-miss avoidance without identity swaps. Reference subject: warehouse forklift pedestrian lane. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: hold a fixed monitoring view; no camera movement; target motion value 0.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Warehouse aisle or yard intersection with forklifts/pedestrian route and readable right-of-way context. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Application value layer: application_type=safety_training. Application objective: Train or evaluate recognition of unsafe industrial states, violations, alarms, and required safe responses. Scenario: Pedestrian enters forklift lane; show warning, braking, and near-miss avoidance without identity swaps. Required observable events: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: warehouse forklift pedestrian lane; the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active. Decision-relevant elements: worker or vehicle position relative to the danger zone (warehouse forklift pedestrian lane); PPE, barrier, signage, interlock, or alarm state; machine state before and after the trigger; reference-image requirement: Warehouse aisle or yard intersection with forklifts/pedestrian route and readable right-of-way context. Application success criteria: a safety reviewer can identify the violation and the required response; the event sequence is complete enough for training or compliance audit; the clip does not invent misleading safe states after a hazardous trigger. Misleading failure modes to penalize: hazard appears without the required alarm or stop consequence; unsafe action is visually softened so the violation becomes ambiguous; scene adds irrelevant people or equipment that changes the decision context.
